reader1.note: Tree-sitter visitors per language fill FunctionEntity/ClassEntity records with name, kind, line_start and line_end, then mappers store them as graph nodes.

reader2.note: Tree-sitter visitors per language build IR entities (name, line_start/line_end) that ir_to_graph stores as graph nodes with kind and path.

reader1.note: About 35 per-language crates (python, rust, go, java, ts, c, cpp...) are all registered in one ParserRegistry dispatch; six extra grammars sit behind the extra-languages feature.

reader2.note: Registry dispatches to about 38 per-language parser crates (python, rust, go, java, ...), each with its own tree-sitter extractor.

reader1.note: FunctionEntity carries signature, parameters, return_type and doc_comment, filled by the language visitors.

reader2.note: FunctionEntity carries signature, parameters, return type and doc_comment, which the mapper stores as node properties.

reader1.note: visibility, is_async, is_static, is_abstract are stored by the parser and queried by find_by_signature (with_modifier) and symbol_info output.

reader2.note: visibility, is_async and is_static are set by parsers, stored as properties and filtered in find_by_signature.

reader1.note: Parsers set is_test from decorators/attributes/annotations and is_test_node also tags by name and path patterns; find_related_tests uses it.

reader2.note: Rust visitor sets is_test from #[test]; is_test_node also tags by name and path patterns, used by related_tests and impact.

reader1.note: Calls edges are stored in the graph and queried both ways by the get_callers, get_callees and get_call_graph tools.

reader2.note: Calls edges stored in the graph; get_callers/get_callees and codegraph_get_call_graph query both directions.

reader1.note: Imports edges between file and module nodes are stored and read by the dependency graph and find_by_imports tools.

reader2.note: Imports/ImportsFrom edges between files; dependency/dependent queries and codegraph_get_dependency_graph read them.

reader1.note: Extends and Implements edges are written by language mappers and read by impact analysis, find_implementors and ai_context.

reader2.note: Extends and Implements edges are created by mappers and read by find_implementors and impact analysis (subclass, implementation).

reader1.note: Phase 2 of resolve_cross_file_imports links unresolved_calls to definitions in other files, but by a global name map (symbol_map) rather than by imports or scope, so only name matching is met.

reader2.note: Cross-file calls are linked from unresolved_calls via a global name-to-symbol map; only the import-symbol phase uses imports, call matching is by name alone.

reader1.note: cluster_symbols does greedy clustering with labels, but over embedding cosine similarity rather than the graph alone, and the result is returned not stored; SCC exists in graph/algorithms.rs but is not labelled modules.

reader2.note: A labelled clustering step exists but it is greedy embedding-similarity over functions, not graph-based, and results are returned not stored; SCC exists only for cycles.

reader1.note: EdgeType::References edges are created for type references (resolve phase 3) and read by dead_imports and impact.

reader2.note: References edges to types are stored (unresolved_type_refs resolved in phase 3) and read by impact and unused-code analysis.

reader1.note: BM25 inverted index over names, docstrings and comments, queried by the codegraph_symbol_search tool.

reader2.note: In-memory inverted index with BM25 weighting over names/docstrings/comments, queried by codegraph_symbol_search.

reader1.note: Symbol embeddings (ONNX bge-small etc.) are computed and compared by cosine similarity in hybrid symbol_search and find_similar; disabled by --graph-only.

reader2.note: Symbol embeddings (bge-small/jina/granite) computed and cosine-searched, blended with BM25 in symbol_search; off with --graph-only.

reader1.note: Camel/snake-case tokenised BM25 plus embeddings find partial and differently-cased names; no prefix, edit-distance or trigram ranking exists (fuzzy only in find_by_imports match mode).

reader2.note: Case-insensitive substring match plus camelCase token splitting is present; no edit-distance/trigram and search_by_name results are unranked.

reader1.note: codegraph_search_by_pattern compiles a regex and returns matching nodes by name, body prefix or docstring scope; no AST-shaped pattern.

reader2.note: codegraph_search_by_pattern compiles a regex and matches name, signature, body or docstring, returning locations.

reader1.note: codegraph-server --mcp starts a stdio MCP server exposing about 40 codegraph_* tools.

reader2.note: --stdio / --serve starts an MCP server exposing about 42 codegraph_* tools.

reader1.note: A clap parser with --workspace, --run-tool/--tool-args (one-shot index + query printing JSON) and --watch exists, but flags rather than separate index and query subcommands.

reader2.note: clap parser with a one-shot --run-tool/--tool-args that indexes and prints JSON, but no index/query subcommands.

reader1.searched: grep -rn axum|hyper|warp|actix|tiny_http|TcpListener in crates/codegraph-server/src and Cargo.toml; only unix socket (--serve/--connect) and stdio found; VS Code webview in vscode/src/views/graphPanel.ts is an editor panel, not a server
reader1.note: No HTTP listener exists; the interactive graph view is a VS Code webview using LSP requests, and the engine socket is a Unix socket for MCP relay.

reader2.note: No HTTP listener; the interactive graph view is a VS Code webview panel, not a browser/port server.

reader1.note: A VS Code extension, a JetBrains plugin and a Visual Studio extension exist, and install-hooks.js installs a pre-edit agent hook that calls the tool.

reader2.note: install-hooks.js registers a Claude Code PreToolUse hook script; VS Code and JetBrains extensions also launch the server.

reader1.note: Several workspaces are indexed into one shared graph.db under per-slug namespaces with a _registry, and impact searches other projects; MCP tools take no repo-name selector.

reader2.note: Several workspace folders are indexed together with per-project namespaced storage, but there is no named registry with per-repo selection in queries.

reader1.note: index_file hashes content and returns Unchanged when the cached hash matches; GraphUpdater re-parses only changed files.

reader2.note: Per-file FNV hash persisted in IndexState; unchanged files are skipped.

reader1.note: notify-based file watchers and a .git/HEAD branch watcher trigger incremental re-index; --watch runs a daemon.

reader2.note: notify RecommendedWatcher triggers re-index; --watch daemon mode keeps the graph fresh.

reader1.note: IndexConfig has default exclude dirs/patterns, reads .codegraphignore, and enforces max_files and max_depth.

reader2.note: Reads .codegraphignore (gitignore-like, no negation), default exclude globs, max_file_size and max_depth.

reader1.note: JSON, CSV, DOT and triples exporters exist as library functions used by an example; no CLI/MCP command writes the graph, only pr_context markdown/JSON via --run-tool.

reader2.note: Library exports DOT, JSON, CSV and RDF triples; the MCP tool writes a markdown architecture doc (export only library-exposed, no CLI subcommand).

reader1.note: DOT emission for nodes and edges plus a VS Code graph panel that renders and exports SVG; no Mermaid.

reader2.note: Emits Graphviz DOT, and the VS Code webview renders and exports SVG of dependency/call graphs.

reader1.note: codegraph_analyze_impact walks callers, references and subclasses backwards (direct plus 2-level indirect) with cross-project consumers.

reader2.note: Walks incoming Calls/References/Extends/Implements edges from a symbol to direct and transitive impacted symbols with severity.

reader1.note: pr_context runs git diff, parses hunk line ranges per file, maps them to changed functions and adds callers and impact.

reader2.note: Runs git diff, parses @@ hunks into changed line ranges per file, maps them to functions with callers and context.

reader1.note: codegraph_find_circular_deps reports import cycles and find_dead_imports reports unused imports; find_unused_code (no inbound edges) is documented as moved to the pro edition.

reader2.note: Dead imports and import cycles are exposed as MCP tools; find_unused_code (moved to pro tool surface) also exists.

reader1.note: Cyclomatic complexity with grade and nesting is computed per function by parsers and reported by codegraph_analyze_complexity; hot_paths adds call-count hotspots.

reader2.note: Cyclomatic complexity computed at parse time, stored per function, and reported with grades by codegraph_analyze_complexity.

reader1.note: get_ai_context assembles source, callers, callees and related symbols under a max_tokens TokenBudget.

reader2.note: get_curated_context/get_ai_context assemble symbols, source, dependencies and memories within a maxTokens budget.
